result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: The general limit for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The post-sale proviso is outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to Section 336a.
Once the Section 337 period has run, a person shall not bring suit to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The same prohibition applies to initiating arbitration or another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The Section 337 period may be extended only pursuant to Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.

claims.claim: Subject to the promissory-note payment proviso, an acknowledgment or promise must be in a writing signed by the party to be charged to constitute sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract for limitations purposes.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby,

claims.claim: A payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due on a promissory note qualifies as an acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract

claims.claim: Such a payment can start a new limitations period on the note.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time

claims.claim: Such a payment does not by itself revive an already barred cause of action.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.

claims.claim: An answer must contain a statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: Section 337 does not itself specify when the four-year period starts for an ordinary written-contract action.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The ordinary-contract clause gives a duration but no triggering event. The timing provisions for post-sale judgments, accounts stated and rescission address different claims.

result.summary: The supplied texts support each claim within the stated scope. The payment rule is limited to promissory notes; the draft does not apply it to credit-card payments generally.
